decision.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its target interest rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and noted that economic activity continues to strengthen.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January suggests that economic activity has continued to strengthen and that the labor market is stabilizing.
changes.explanation: The Fed updated its view of the labor market from abating deterioration to stabilizing.

changes.quote: Business spending on equipment and software has risen significantly.
changes.explanation: The Fed highlighted stronger spending by businesses on equipment and software.

changes.quote: However, investment in nonresidential structures is declining, housing starts have been flat at a depressed level, and employers remain reluctant to add to payrolls.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that building investment is still dropping and hiring remains weak.

changes.quote: To provide support to mortgage lending and housing markets and to improve overall conditions in private credit markets, the Federal Reserve has been purchasing $1.25 trillion of agency mortgage-backed securities and about $175 billion of agency debt; those purchases are nearing completion, and the remaining transactions will be executed by the end of this month.
changes.explanation: The Fed confirmed that its large-scale mortgage-backed security purchases are wrapping up by the end of the month.

changes.quote: In light of improved functioning of financial markets, the Federal Reserve has been closing the special liquidity facilities that it created to support markets during the crisis.
changes.explanation: Emergency crisis lending programs are being shut down because financial markets are working better.

tone_quotes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January suggests that economic activity has continued to strengthen and that the labor market is stabilizing.
With substantial resource slack continuing to restrain cost pressures and longer-term inflation expectations stable, inflation is likely to be subdued for some time.

The Committee will maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and continues to anticipate that economic conditions, including low rates of resource utilization, subdued inflation trends, and stable inflation expectations, are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for an extended period.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.6% APR costs about $56.67 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.66% and moved -5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.97% would fall by about $9.14 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 9.8%, and employers added an average of -117k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.2% over the past year (February 2010); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -3 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.4% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the federal funds rate will likely stay exceptionally low for an extended period. Educational forecast models suggest a 60% chance of a hold at the next meeting.
